newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Arafat open to all options for peace in Middle East.
newsitem.headline: Arafat open to all options for peace in Middle East.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Monday accused Israel of dishonest intentions in implementing the peace accord, but said he was still open to all options to end the stalemate in the Middle East.
"I am looking to achieve real peace in the land of peace. I am asking for an accurate and honest implementation of what has been signed and agreed upon," Arafat told a public meeting in Colombo.

"All the options are open. I am sure the international community will not leave us alone because now peace is not only a Palestinian need, it is an Israeli need and an international need," Arafat said.
"I am asking the international community to protect the peace of the brave," he said.
Arafat, who arrived in Sri Lanka for a 24-hour visit from Islamabad, said he sought peace despite recent tragedies as the alternative was even more horrible.

"We talk about peace in spite of tragedies because we know the alternative is a real disaster in the Middle East, not only for us but for the whole area," he told the meeting at a luxury hotel overlooking Colombo's Galle Face promenade.

Arafat, facing a diplomatic crisis with Israel over its plan to build a new settlement in Arab east Jerusalem, has been accused by Tel Aviv of giving a "green light" to militants to launch attacks on the Jewish state.
When asked to comment on the Israeli accusation, Arafat said: "This is a silly point. I am not ready to respond to silly questions."
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy on Monday blasted Arafat for pleading his case before world bodies instead of negotiating with Israel.
"Arafat must understand that problems won't be solved in international areanas...he must be here, to decide which path he takes," Levy said.
"He hasn't the right to give me orders," an indignant Arafat said in Colombo.
Arafat is on a diplomatic tour that will take him to Bangladesh after Sri Lanka, where he arrived from Pakistan.
Levy's comments came after Arafat told an Islamic summit in Islamabad on Sunday that Israeli policies were bringing the Middle East peace process to a dead end.
"We are surprised by the Israeli decision to isolate and Judaise Jerusalem, constructing new settlements not only inside but outside it," he told the summit.
"The holy land is for use of Christians and Moslems," he said in Colombo.
